Class JsonStreamReader

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.json.JsonStreamReader
public final class JsonStreamReader extends Object

Reads a document value by value, as typed reads. The parser validated the whole document before the first read, so reading never finds invalid JSON: it fails only on a value of a type other than the one read, with a JsonMappingException, or on a call out of order, with an IllegalStateException.

reader.beginObject();
while (reader.hasNextMember()) {
    switch (reader.name(NAMES)) { // NAMES = JsonNames.of("id", "tags")
        case 0 -> id = reader.readLong();
        case 1 -> tags = readTags(reader);
        default -> reader.skipValue();
    }
}

Skipping a value costs the same whatever its size. A reader is not thread-safe.

Since:
0.1.0

    • peekTag

      public int peekTag(JsonNames member, JsonNames tags)
      Returns the index of the tag that names the type of the next value, an object, from the string value of its tag member, wherever the member is among the others; the reader stays at the object. The code generated for a sealed interface laid out with JsonTagMember reads the object as the record the tag names.
      Parameters:
      member - the name of the tag member, the only one in its JsonNames
      tags - the tags
      Returns:
      the index of the tag in tags
      Throws:
      JsonMappingException - if the next value is not an object, or has no tag member, or one whose value is not one of tags
      IllegalStateException - if the reader is not at a value

      public void skipUnknownMember(JsonNames names)
